segments.text: We are going to trace bubble sort on the array 3, 1, 2.
The goal is to sort this array in ascending order.
Bubble sort works by comparing adjacent elements and swapping them if they are out of order.
We will show each comparison and swap step by step.
In the first pass, we start by comparing the first two elements, 3 and 1.
Since 3 is greater than 1, they are out of order.
We perform an inflate swap.
Now the array is 1, 3, 2.
Notice that no values were lost or added.
Next, we compare the next adjacent pair, 3 and 2.
Since 3 is greater than 2, we swap them again.
The array is now 1, 2, 3.
This completes the first pass.
The largest element, 3, has bubbled to the end.
In the second pass, we compare the first two elements again, 1 and 2.
Since 1 is less than 2, they are already in order.
No swap is needed.
This confirms that the array is sorted.
Pass-based sorting stops when no swaps occur in a full pass.
The final sorted array is 1, 2, 3.
We have verified that the values are in ascending order and that no values were lost or added during the process.
This matches the original problems requirement to sort 3, 1, 2.
To recap, bubble-sort uses pass-based sorting to repeatedly compare and swap adjacent elements.
We started with 3, 1, 2, swap to get 1, 3, 2, then 1, 2, 3 and confirmed no further swaps were needed.
The final array is sorted and all steps were justified by the comparison rule.
